thread:
maria: Quick proposal — we should run a tightly controlled apples-to-apples set to isolate the perf regression from last week. I think three axes matter: kernel selection, batching heuristics, and KV-cache warm vs cold.

kevin: SG. Can you list the exact factors and the minimal matrix? want to avoid combinatorial explosion. :eyes:

maria: Minimal matrix idea: same model checkpoint, identical prompt set (2000 prompts from prod-sample v2), identical decoding params (temp=0.2, top_p=0.95, max_new_tokens=128, stop=["\n\n"], tokenizer-aligned inputs (pre-tokenize and compare token counts), and run replay harness + synthetic steady load for each config.

sanjay: Important: ensure kv-cache warm path is exercised. For warm vs cold, do 3-shot warm (prime with prior tokens) vs fresh sessions. Also record kv cache hit ratios per request.

alex: For kernel selection we should validate both the runtime's default kernel-picker and a forced-kernel run (explicit kernel flags) so we can attribute differences to kernel choice vs scheduling.

jamie: can we keep batching constant? e.g. batch_size=8, max_latency=100ms? Or do we sweep batch_size [1,4,8] only if default change doesn't explain it.

maria: Plan: start with single-run apples (forced kernelA vs kernelB) at batch=8, synthetic steady QPS that matches our 95th-percentile prod shape. Steps: 1) Replay harness (original traffic) 2) Synth harness (same length/dist but randomized timing) 3) Profiling traces (nvtx + runtime internal counters) 4) Aggregate p50/p95/p99 token-latencies + decode time + kernel time breakdown + kv metrics.

kevin: Can you paste the commands? easier to copy-config into CI job.

maria: Commands (draft):
```bash
# replay harness
./harness/replay_run --model=redwood-xl-1 --checkpoint=sha1:bd3f2a --prompts=prod-sample-v2.jsonl --decoding='temp=0.2,top_p=0.95,max_new_tokens=128' --batch=8 --force-kernel=auto --kv-mode=warm --out=out/replay_auto_warm.jsonl

# forced kernelB
./harness/replay_run --model=redwood-xl-1 --checkpoint=sha1:bd3f2a --prompts=prod-sample-v2.jsonl --decoding='temp=0.2,top_p=0.95,max_new_tokens=128' --batch=8 --force-kernel=kernelB --kv-mode=warm --out=out/replay_kernelB_warm.jsonl
```

sanjay: Add flags for tracing: --trace=nvtx --runtime-counters=true and ensure we capture KV cache size per request.

alex: For synth harness: use the same token-length distribution but with Poisson inter-arrival to approximate bursts. Config snippet:
```json
{"qps": 120, "arrival": "poisson", "length_dist": "prod_sample_v2_tokens.json"}
```

jamie: Metrics we need in the dashboard: decode_time_per_token, kernel_compute_time, kernel_select_reason (why chosen), batch_fill_rate, kv_cache_hit, p50/p95/p99 tail. Also record deterministic seed used for tokenizer alignment.

maria: Perf-regression hypothesis: recent kernel selector change (commit f2c3a9) sometimes picks kernelB which increases per-token compute for short sequences due to missing fused attention kernel. If true, forcing kernelA should restore previous p95. We'll validate.

kevin: If we see kernelB cost only on short sequences, that points to kernel selection policy thresholds. Could be cutover point in sequence length heuristics.

jamie: Also watch for batching heuristics: if batch assembly waits to fill to 8 but latency SLO forces early flushes, effective batch sizes drop and kernel behavior shifts. Capture actual batch sizes distribution.

maria: CI integration: I can add a nightly job that runs a reduced-size apples test (200 prompts) and uploads aggregated metrics + flamegraphs to perf-bucket. Then trigger full run on-demand.

ci-bot: Build 6078 for harness pushed by @maria. Artifacts: s3://perf-bucket/6078/artifacts.zip.

alex: Good. After initial runs, let's do a compare table: replay_auto_warm vs replay_kernelB_warm vs synth_auto_cold. We'll diff decode speed, kernel breakdown, and tokenizer token counts to ensure input parity.

sanjay: Also add a deterministic stop-sequence test: run with and without stop to check how early stopping changes batch behavior.

kevin: Timeline? if we get CI job + scripts today, we can run heavyweight passes tomorrow and produce a short write-up for eng-sync on Friday.

maria: I'll open a PR with harness changes and a checklist for the run. Assigning tasks: @kevin to add kernel-forcing support to the runner, @sanjay to add kv metrics hooks, @alex to prepare synth config, @jamie to draft dashboard widgets. I'll post PR link here once ready.

jamie: :thumbsup:

maria: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/harness/pull/142 (draft) — please review.

kevin: reviewing now. initial glance: looks clean. If tests pass, start the small-run.

ci-bot: Harness tests 142/Unit passed, integration queued.

maria: Thanks — will trigger small-run after integration passes.

alex: One final ask: log tokenizer pre/post token counts in the same csv row as latency so we can quickly filter mismatched inputs.

maria: noted. I'll add that to the PR.

jamie: Cool. We'll regroup after the runs and decide whether it's kernel policy or batching heuristic follow-up. :mag_right:
